audit_findings.A_exact_protection: Asserts `git status --short` is empty for exactly these 3 paths. It does not protect any other file, including .github/workflows/*.yml.
audit_findings.B_why_created: Added in commit 3aaa7401 (Post-Integration Interpretive & Applied Intelligence Contract, N-1-era). Purpose stated in that phase's spec: backend intelligence-pipeline work sessions (Evidence/Claim/Report Engine layers) must never accidentally touch the live Public site build or its committed data -- a guard against an intelligence-phase session silently breaking the production daily.yml pipeline while building unrelated backend modules.
audit_findings.D_full_public_site_freeze: Only for the briefing.py/site/data paths specifically -- not a freeze on 'the public site' as a concept, since site/ is itself fully regenerated by briefing.py and is gitignored (never committed to main at all; see .gitignore line 1). The real protected surface is: briefing.py's source code, and anything that would land in git status under data/.
audit_findings.F_blocks_new_independent_routes: Not inherently -- the test only checks git status on those 3 paths. A new route added by modifying briefing.py would trip it (because briefing.py's content changes); a new route added by a script that runs AFTER briefing.py and writes only into the gitignored site/ directory, without ever importing or calling briefing.py, does not touch any of the 3 protected paths in a way git tracks (site/ is gitignored, so site/intelligence/** never shows in `git status`either).
audit_findings.G_temporary_safety_device: Appears intentionally durable (carried through N-1 through N-4B unmodified, several Te-approved phases referencing it), not a throwaway one-phase check.
audit_findings.H_conflicts_with_n5: No real conflict once Priority 1 is used: N-5 asks to connect Public delivery to the real site build without widening blast radius on the live cron pipeline. The freeze's actual purpose (protect briefing.py source + git-tracked data) is fully compatible with writing generated pages into the gitignored site/ directory via a separate script invoked by the workflow, rather than by briefing.py itself.

integration_options_considered.option: Independent build step: a separate script (public_delivery.py's own __main__ entrypoint) run as an extra shell line in .github/workflows/daily.yml, AFTER `python briefing.py build` has produced site/ and BEFORE the gh-pages commit. briefing.py is never imported by, nor imports, this script.
Extension hook/plugin system inside briefing.py's build().
integration_options_considered.reason: No such hook exists in briefing.py; adding one would itself be a briefing.py modification, same freeze violation as direct wiring.

integration_options_considered.option: Explicit allowlist carve-out inside test_56 for site/intelligence/** only.
integration_options_considered.but: unnecessary -- site/ is gitignored entirely, so test_56's git-status-based check never sees anything under site/intelligence/** regardless; no carve-out is needed.

integration_options_considered.reason: Not needed; Priority 1 fully satisfies the goal without touching the contract.

reason: Priority 1 achieves full Public Intelligence Page delivery (real site/intelligence/** pages built from the real Report Engine, in the real daily.yml build) with zero bytes changed in briefing.py, zero bytes changed in test_56_public_unchanged, and zero new files landing in git-tracked data/. The only file touched to wire this in is .github/workflows/daily.yml, which is outside test_56's protected_scope and was never claimed to be frozen by any prior phase.
risk: The new workflow step runs inside the existing 'build' job's single long-lived shell step, after site/ already exists and before the gh-pages push. It is wrapped with a shell-level `|| echo ...` fallback so a Python exception there cannot fail the job or block the gh-pages publish (mirrors this workflow's existing fail-soft pattern used for the photo-collection and inbox steps). Worst case on failure: site/intelligence/ is simply missing for that run, with no effect on any other page.
rollback_path: Revert the one added line in .github/workflows/daily.yml (does not touch briefing.py or the freeze test). public_delivery.py remains a correct, independently tested, standalone module either way.
